title: RCMP officer cleared in shooting death of B.C. activist that sparked Anonymous revenge campaign
subtitle: James McIntyre, 48, was shot and killed by a single police bullet July 16, 2015, during a confrontation with two RCMP officers in Dawson Creek
article: An RCMP officer has been cleared of culpability in last year's shooting death of a protester in Dawson Creek, B.C., in an incident that sparked a campaign of cyberattacks, hacking and leaking of government secrets by Anonymous, the global hacktivist group.

James McIntyre, 48, was shot and killed by a single police bullet July 16, 2015, during a confrontation with two RCMP officers called to a disturbance at a public meeting about a massive hydroelectric project planned for the Peace River in northeastern B.C.

At the time, Anonymous said McIntyre was one of theirs and unleashed a headline-grabbing vendetta, shutting down police websites, threatening to reveal private information about officers and leaking top-secret documents it hacked from the federal Cabinet.
On Wednesday, the Independent Investigations Office of B.C., which investigates officer-involved shootings, released its report clearing the RCMP of wrongdoing.

The IIO also released a photo of the Anonymous protest mask, the stylized face of Guy Fawkes, McIntyre was wearing when shot, confirming what authorities would not previously confirm. Another photo shows a switchblade and a dagger McIntyre was carrying.

Police were called for a disturbance at the Stonebridge Hotel in Dawson Creek at 6:34 p.m. McIntyre, his face covered by the mask and with one hand behind his back, met the officers outside the hotel when they arrived at 6:57 p.m.
"Officers noted the affected person was carrying a switchblade," the report says. Over the police radio, officers could be heard saying "drop it now," "put the knife down" and "put it down now."
At 7:16 an officer says: "One male down, shot."
Seven minutes later an ambulance arrived.
The report says McIntyre opened the knife and moved towards the officers; several civilian witnesses told the IIO he was "lunging," "jabbing at" and "coming towards" the officers.
The report does not name McIntyre or the officers. McIntyre is referred to as "the affected person," the RCMP shooter as "the subject officer" and the second RCMP officer as the "witness officer."

The witness officer told investigators that as McIntyre approached, he could see his eyes and decided to pepper spray him, thinking it would "defuse the threat right there, and he would most likely go on his knees, and then we can proceed to take the knife away from him."
Instead, it enraged him. He yelled "you fucker," and charged at the officer, the officer told investigators. The officer took cover and he saw McIntyre change focus to his partner.
The witness officer then "heard a pop" and saw McIntyre drop.

"The guy was still looking to put up a fight, even though he's been shot," the witness officer said. He saw a second knife in McIntyre's back pocket and moved in to retrieve it and then helped handcuff him, he said.

A civilian witness told investigators that McIntyre did not immediately fall. He took a couple of steps back, still in a "defiant stance," the report quotes a witness saying. "He finally crumpled alongside a post."
A third officer brought a medical kit and was trying to locate the "profuse arterial bleeding" by cutting away his jeans when an ambulance arrived.
The subject officer - the officer who fired the fatal shot - declined to be interviewed by the IIO, as is his right, the report says.

"As of the time this decision is being issued, it does not appear that the subject officer has completed any reports or notes of his recollection of the incident. The IIO has, and continues to engage with the RCMP on the necessity of officers completing timely reports."

An autopsy said the 9mm bullet entered McIntyre's body in the pelvic area on his right side. As it travelled to its point of rest in the left buttocks area, it tore the right femoral artery and vein, causing death through massive blood loss.
The IIO probe focused on whether the officer was legally justified in shooting McIntyre.

Investigators looked at the Twitter account of @jaymack9, which is believed to be McIntyre's. One of his last tweets, sent the day of the shooting, read: "Anonymous splinter group 2 attend the scheduled meeting in Dawson Creek tonight."

The IIO concluded the two officers "were confronted with threatening and potentially deadly assaultive acts involving a non-trivial weapon. The threat was undeniably real and imminent," the report says.
"In those circumstances, it would be unreasonable to conclude that the ultimate use of deadly force - a single gunshot not aimed at the centre of mass - was unnecessary or disproportionate."

Last year, in a face-to-face interview by the National Post with the spokesman for the Anonymous crew who ran the leaks campaign, the hacktivists said they would retaliate if the shooting was covered up.

"Our message to whoever will be making those kind of decisions (is) that we are a very talented and patient and courageous crew and even if it takes us many months or many years to figure out what went wrong, we will sniff out your dirtiest laundry, procure it from wherever it's hiding and find the highest flagpole in the windiest part of the public square and hang it up for everyone to smell and everyone to see," he said.
